title: "02_clean"
format: html
editor: visual

## Intention

The data given has the variables Gene_symbol, Probe_ID, and different samples. We would like have samples as unique observations in each row and gene having its own column.

We use these files:

input: datafile loaded\
output file: 01_dat_load.tsv

## Libraries

```{r}
library("tidyverse")
library("readr")
library("here")
```

## Load file

```{r}

batchCN_array_combined <- read_tsv(here("data/01_batchCN_array_combined_load.tsv"))

```

## Clean data

Checking manually to see how everything looks.

```{r}
head(batchCN_array_combined)
```

To tidy the data we want to make the observations, that is the samples, into rows and the variables (genes) into columns.

Right now each row has a gene, and the collums are probe IDs and sample variables. First we try to see any genes are repeated.

```{r}
batchCN_array_combined |> 
  group_by(Gene_symbol) |> 
  summarise(n = n()) |> 
  arrange(desc(n))
```

The genes being repeated means there are samples with multiple expression values, for the same gene. This is because there has been used different probes for each gene-sample pair, so we have multiple sets of expressions.

We have chosen to take the mean for each gene-sample expressions, to not loose any data.

We first group the genes, and nest the data for each gene. To visualize, we look at a single gene.

```{r}
batchCN_array_combined |> 
  group_by(Gene_symbol) |> 
  nest() |> 
  filter(Gene_symbol == "RERE") |> 
  unnest()
```

Now we want to privot the data so we are able to stratify on sample ID.

```{r}
batchCN_array_combined |> 
  group_by(Gene_symbol) |> 
  nest() |> 
  filter(Gene_symbol == "RERE") |> 
  mutate(data = map(.x = data,
                    .f = ~pivot_longer(.x,
                                       cols = starts_with("SAMPLE"),
                                       names_to = "Sample_ID",
                                       values_to = "Sample_expression"
        ))) |> 
  unnest()
```

Summarize the data by sample ID and get the average expression.

```{r}
batchCN_array_combined |> 
  group_by(Gene_symbol) |> 
  nest() |> 
  filter(Gene_symbol == "RERE") |> 
  mutate(data = map(.x = data,
                    .f = ~pivot_longer(.x,
                                       cols = starts_with("SAMPLE"),
                                       names_to = "Sample_ID",
                                       values_to = "Sample_expression"
                    ))) |> 
  mutate(data = map(.x = data,
                    .f = ~summarize(.x, 
                                    Avr_Ex = mean(Sample_expression),
                                    .by = Sample_ID)
         )) |> 
  unnest()
```

Now we are do it on the whole data set, not just a single gene.

```{r}
avr_probe_batchCN_array_combined <- batchCN_array_combined |> 
  group_by(Gene_symbol) |> 
  nest() |> 
  mutate(data = map(.x = data,
                    .f = ~pivot_longer(.x,
                                       cols = starts_with("SAMPLE"),
                                       names_to = "Sample_ID",
                                       values_to = "Sample_expression"
                    ))) |> 
  mutate(data = map(.x = data,
                    .f = ~summarize(.x, 
                                    Avr_Ex = mean(Sample_expression),
                                    .by = Sample_ID)
  )) |> 
  unnest(cols = c(data))
```

```{r}
avr_probe_batchCN_array_combined
```

The values from different probes have been averaged out.

There are still some issues. Some of the sample IDs have "Replicate" in their name, so some samples are repeated!

```{r}
avr_probe_batchCN_array_combined |> 
  filter(str_ends(Sample_ID, "Replicate"))
```

We take the mean of the repeat values with the original values across the genes.

```{r}
rep_removed_avr_probe_batchCN_array_combined <- avr_probe_batchCN_array_combined |> 
  mutate(Sample_ID = str_remove(Sample_ID, " Replicate")) |> 
  group_by(Sample_ID, Gene_symbol) |> 
  summarize(Value_Corrected = mean(Avr_Ex))
```

```{r}
rep_removed_avr_probe_batchCN_array_combined
```

Now each sample is a unique observation. We would still like to make each sample have its own row and the genes have its own columns.

```{r}
tidy_CN_array_combined <- rep_removed_avr_probe_batchCN_array_combined |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = Gene_symbol,
              values_from = Value_Corrected)
```

```{r}
tidy_CN_array_combined |> 
  slice_head(n = 10)
```

Now the data is much more tidy.

## Separate by tissue type

Old code

```{r}
batchCN_tidy <- batchCN_array_combined |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(Gene_symbol, Probe_Id),
    names_to = "Sample",
    values_to = "Expression"
  ) |> 
  group_by(Sample, Gene_symbol) |>  
  summarise(
    Expression = mean(Expression, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
    ) |> 
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Gene_symbol,
    values_from = Expression
  )
```

```{r}
head(batchCN_tidy)
```

Take the average of replicate samples

```{r}
batchCN_tidy_rmrep <- batchCN_tidy |> 
  mutate(
    Sample = str_remove(Sample, "^SAMPLE\\s+")
    ) |> 
  mutate(
    Sample = str_remove(Sample, "\\s+Replicate$")
    ) |> 
  group_by(Sample) |> 
  summarise(
    across(where(is.numeric), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    .groups = "drop"
    ) 
```

```{r}
head(batchCN_tidy_rmrep)
```

We want to separate tissue type from Sample.

```{r}
batchCN_tidy_rmrep_clean <- batchCN_tidy_rmrep |> 
  mutate(
    Tissue_type = word(Sample,2)
    ) |> 
  mutate(
    Sample = word(Sample,1)
    ) |> 
  relocate(Tissue_type)
```

```{r}
(batchCN_tidy_rmrep_clean)
```

## Save the cleaned data

```{r}
write_tsv(batchCN_tidy_rmrep_clean,
          here("data/02_dat_clean.tsv"))
```
